title: Small Costs Add Up
objective: After this level you can explain how small recurring costs like subscriptions add up over a year.
summary: People guessed they spent $86 a month on subscriptions; the real average was $219. Small recurring costs hide month to month and add up over a year, and every one has an opportunity cost.

cards.headline: Guess what you spend on subscriptions each month. Now more than double it.
cards.body: In a 2022 C+R Research survey of 1,000 US consumers, people guessed $86 a month. When they listed every subscription, the average came to $219.

cards.headline: Why small costs hide
cards.body: A subscription asks for your attention once, then charges quietly every month with nothing to hand over at a till. In the same survey, 74% said recurring charges were easy to forget, and 42% had stopped using a subscription but forgot they were still paying for it. That's money buying precisely nothing.

cards.headline: Multiply by twelve
cards.body: Small costs look small because we meet them one month at a time. The survey's gap between guess and reality was $133 a month. Over 12 months, that's $1,596. Same money, very different feeling.

cards.fact: $5 a day sounds like nothing. $1,250 a year sounds like a vacation.
cards.context: An economics textbook example: spending $5 a day more on a bought lunch than one from home adds up to $1,250 over 250 workdays, perhaps the cost of a decent vacation. That's Level 15's opportunity cost, scaled up. Describing the cost as "a nice vacation" instead of "$5 a day" might lead to a different choice.

mascot.line: Nobody misses $5. Plenty of people would miss a vacation.

cards.headline: Small costs: added up
learned: People guessed $86 a month; the real figure was $219
Recurring charges are easy to forget
Multiply monthly costs by 12 to see them
$5 a day is a vacation a year

questions.prompt: In the 2022 survey, how did people's guesses about their subscription spending compare with reality?

options.label: They guessed too high
options.rationale: Reality came in higher, not lower.

options.label: Most had no subscriptions
options.rationale: They averaged $219 a month in subscriptions.

questions.explanation: People guessed $86 a month; itemized, the average was $219.

questions.prompt: Why can a small recurring cost feel smaller than it really is?

options.label: Recurring charges shrink over time
options.rationale: The charge stays the same each month.

options.label: We see it one month at a time, not added up over a year
Banks refund small charges automatically
options.rationale: Nobody refunds a subscription you forgot.

options.label: Small charges aren't counted in a budget
options.rationale: A budget lists every bill and expense.

questions.explanation: Seen monthly, $133 feels small. Over 12 months it's $1,596.

questions.prompt: From Level 15: in the lunch example, what is the opportunity cost of buying lunch out all year?

options.label: The $5 extra paid each day
options.rationale: That's the money cost. The opportunity cost is what it could have bought.

options.label: The tax on each meal
options.rationale: Tax is part of the money cost.

options.label: The vacation the $1,250 could have paid for
The cook's wages
options.rationale: That's the café's cost, not yours.

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up: here, a vacation's worth of spending.
